name: hungry-young-debut-register
style: 1994 East Coast boom-bap demo tape, raw and hungry. Young male rapper about nineteen, higher slightly nasal voice with a raw cracking edge, fast eager flow pushing ahead of the kick, gasping a quick breath at every line end, dry close mic, rap only. Swung 12-bit sampler drums at 92 BPM, crunchy aliased snare, round filtered bassline, chopped dusty piano stab on loop, vinyl crackle, near-mono cassette mix, lo-fi grit.
exclude: trap hi-hats, 808 slides, auto-tune, melodic singing, sung chorus, deep baritone, polished modern mix, orchestral strings
lyrics:
[Intro: young voice, half-spoken, eager]
Uh. Uh-huh.
Money printer manual. Page one. Take notes.

[Verse: fast, hungry, rushing the beat, sharp breath at each line end]
Number one: never tell 'em what you printed,
trillions out the back door, keep the ledger tinted.

Number four: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

Number six: no credit? Nah, they live on the slate,
and you're paying it back in the price on your plate.

Number seven: keep the family out the business,
Treasury and the bank in one bed, God as my witness.

Number ten: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout on tick and they ain't paid at all.

[Outro: beat drops to the piano stab, out of breath]
And the fix, from the future? Easy.
No hand on the printer.

[End]
